dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?

Yeah, hi, good morning. My name is Leo Santoro. I'm calling about the plowing, the plow came down my street and, uh, it buried the end of my driveway. A wall of snow, I'm telling you, it's like a wall.
Oh, I'm sorry to hear that, Mr. Santoro. Let me get some details. Can you give me the address where this happened?
One ninety-one Bliss Road. Over by Easton's Beach, the beach side of the neighborhood.
One ninety-one Bliss Road. Got it. And the plow came through after the storm, or during it?

During, after, I don't know, it went by maybe two hours ago. This is the snow that came in Sunday and then turned to rain, it finished up today. So now it's that heavy wet stuff, pesado, you know, like cement. Sorry. Heavy.
No need to apologize. So it's the heavy, wet snow, and it's packed across the end of your driveway.

Right. Right across the whole mouth of it. I shoveled out the driveway already, the whole thing, and then the plow comes and puts it all back. Todo de vuelta. Everything back. Sorry. I did it twice now, my back is not happy.
That's frustrating, I understand. What you're describing is the berm the plow leaves at the curb. So you're asking for a plow to come back by and clear it?
Yes. Can somebody come back? Just, you know, a pass, clear the end of it. I can't lift that, it's wet and it's like a foot and a half high.
Okay. Let me write that down. A foot and a half, across the driveway entrance at 191 Bliss Road. Is the street itself passable otherwise?
The street is fine, it's plowed. It's just my driveway got the gift. [pause] Hold on one second, my cousin is on the other line, he's calling me from Providence, he's giving me advice. Hold on.
Sure, take your time.

Okay, I'm back. He says I should tell you the plow guy has to come back. He says in Providence they do it. I told him this is Newport, it's different. Anyway, he's talking in my ear, I can't hear you good, let me put him on hold. Un momento. Okay.
No problem. I'm still here. Do you want me to repeat anything?
No, no. So what do you do? Somebody comes back?

What I can do is put in a request with the crew supervisors for a return pass on Bliss Road. I can't tell you an exact time, because the crews are still working through the whole city right now with the storm just ending. But it goes on the list with your address and what you've told me.
A list. How long is the list?
I couldn't tell you that from here. It's a busy morning. They tend to take care of the main roads first and then go back for the side streets and the cleanup.
Okay. I understand that. But it's not the street I'm complaining, it's the end of the driveway. Every time, the same thing. The guy comes, boom, wall.
I hear you. And I'll note that on the request, that the berm is blocking the driveway entrance. Is there anyone in the house who needs to get out, like for a medical appointment or work?
No, no, nothing like that. I just want my car out sometime today. Maybe I go to the store. Tengo que, uh, I need milk. Sorry, I go back and forth when I'm annoyed.

That's all right. So no emergency, but you'd like to get your car out today. Let me read it back to make sure I have it right. Leo Santoro, 191 Bliss Road, near Easton's Beach. The plow left a heavy wall of snow at the end of your driveway, about a foot and a half high, and you'd like a plow to come back and clear it. Is that right?
That's right. That's all of it.
And the best number to reach you if the crew has questions?
It's 401-555-0183. This is my cell.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-three. Okay.
Yeah. [pause] Hold on, my cousin is saying something again. He says ask if I can put the snow on the other side of the street. I said no, I can't do that, that's crazy.
Right, I'd say don't push it into the roadway. That can cause problems for the plows and for traffic. If you can, pile it on your own property, on either side of the driveway.
I know, I know. I was only telling you what he said. He doesn't live here. He lives in a place with a parking lot.
Well, tell him thank you for the advice anyway.
I'll tell him. He'll love that. [pause] So okay, you put the request in. And somebody calls me?

The request goes to the crew supervisor. If they need anything they'll call you at that number. Otherwise you'll probably just see the plow come by. If it's still not cleared by this evening, call us back and mention that you already put in a request this morning.
This evening, okay. And if I call back, you have the note?
It'll be in the system under your address, yes. Anyone who picks up can see it.
Okay. Good. Because last time, I didn't call, I just waited, and nobody came. So now I call.
That's the right thing to do. Is there anything else I can help you with this morning?
No, that's it. Just the driveway. Thank you, Lorraine. Gracias. Sorry, thank you.
You're welcome, Mr. Santoro. Take it easy with that shoveling, and don't overdo it on the wet snow. Have a good day.
You too. Bye now.
